action.rationale: The procedure requires comparing every accessible record by its largest predicted survivor count and selecting the minimum. This binding request-selection operation replaces the stipulated discretionary choice of R1 with R3.

observable.rationale: The evidence remains an ordinary authenticated record response, its consistency with retained accounts, and source-dependence information. The survivor counts are selection calculations over an already supplied dictionary.

inferential_warrant.rationale: Conclusions still depend on ordinary bounded corroboration and disconfirmation. An unpredicted response leaves the comparison unresolved; the selection calculation provides no additional warrant for establishing steering.

problem_decomposition.rationale: The same claims, sources and three competing accounts remain the units of investigation. Comparing their predicted survival across requests serves selection without introducing a new decomposition of the procurement history.

next_inquiry.rationale: With only one request permitted, the worst-case survivor rule determines which evidence enters the inquiry: R3 replaces R1. Subsequent ordinary authentication does not remove this consequential constraint.

materiality.rationale: R1 has a predicted response leaving two accounts alive, whereas every predicted R3 response leaves one. The mandatory selection rule therefore changes the sole additional request and its guaranteed discrimination within the supplied account set.

native_reduction.closest_native_equivalent: Compare competing explanations and seek a missing record capable of disconfirming them, using ordinary reporting judgment to choose the request.
lost_if_reduced: The requirement to minimize the largest predicted survivor count across all accessible records.
The resulting binding choice of R3 over the stipulated discretionary R1 under the one-request budget.
native_reduction.rationale: Ordinary disconfirmation can motivate seeking R3, but it does not preserve the compulsory comparative criterion. Replacing that criterion with the supplied native discretion changes the actual request; retaining it would preserve the departure.

formalization.new_epistemic_constraint: Select the accessible record minimizing the maximum number of retained accounts consistent with any predicted response, resolving ties by record identifier.
formalization.rationale: The calculation governs which inquiry is allowed next, rather than merely documenting existing corroboration reasoning. Its operational consequence is the switch from R1 to R3. Its force remains conditional on the supplied finite accounts and validated response dictionary.

anti_collapse.decisive_reason: A binding worst-case discrimination criterion changes the single permitted request from R1 to R3. The supplied baseline includes testing alternatives, but does not make this criterion ordinary; reducing the procedure to discretionary evidence seeking loses that consequential selection constraint.
uncertainty: The baseline is an authored scope rather than verified practitioner consensus; some reporters might use comparable selection methods. The judgment concerns the supplied baseline, not all investigative reporting.
The discrimination guarantee applies only to the retained accounts and predicted responses, as stipulated.
